summary.name: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
summary.one_liner: An arXiv research paper introducing generative agents, software agents that use a large language model with memory, reflection, and planning to simulate believable human behavior in a Sims-inspired sandbox town.
use_cases: prototyping interactive characters for games or environments
researching emergent social behavior among AI agents
reading about memory, reflection and planning in LLM agents
summary.what_it_does: The paper introduces generative agents, computational software agents that simulate believable human behavior. The architecture extends a large language model to store a complete record of an agent's experiences in natural language, synthesizes those memories into higher-level reflections over time, and retrieves them dynamically to plan behavior. The authors populate an interactive sandbox inspired by The Sims with twenty-five agents that end users can talk to in natural language. In their evaluation, a single user-specified idea (a Valentine's Day party) led agents to spread invitations, form acquaintances, ask each other out, and arrive at the party together. An ablation study reports that observation, planning, and reflection each contribute to believability.
notable: Architecture of observation, planning, and reflection on top of a large language model
Interactive sandbox town of twenty-five agents inspired by The Sims
Ablation study showing each component contributes to believability
Emergent behaviors such as invitations and coordinated party attendance
caveats: The page is only an arXiv abstract and listing; no code or license terms are stated on this page
Evaluation is described in the abstract only; details are not on this page
